text:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: elevated 5xx rate from model-serving runtime in us-west1. Metric: gateway_5xx_rate > 5% for 3m. Routing to #incidents and paging @alex (oncall).

alex (oncall): Acked. pinging eng-runtime and SRE. creating incident channel. any initial impact metrics?

incident-bot: Auto-notes: affected services: redwood-hosted-api (generation & chat endpoints). Estimated requests failing: ~12% over last 10m. Errors: 502/503/504 and timeouts.

sam (eng-runtime): I'm attached. seeing spike in model runner 5xx and repeated container restarts on a subset of GPU nodes (us-west1-gpu-pool-3). Looks like OOMs leading to segfaults in model_runner process.

maria (sre): Can you paste the recent pod logs + dmesg? also checking node-level OOM/kern logs.

sam (eng-runtime): pulling logs. snippet:```
[2026-03-15T21:12:03Z] model_runner[pid=4412]: allocation failed: requested 1.6G, available 0.0G
[2026-03-15T21:12:03Z] model_runner[pid=4412]: panic: segfault at 0x0
[2026-03-15T21:12:03Z] kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 4412 (model_runner) total-vm:8192764kB, anon-rss:7300000kB
```

olivia (eng-infra): Node level shows GPU driver reset events around the same timestamps. nvlink errors + nvgpu watchdog triggered.

dave (eng-platform): Traffic graph shows retry storms on gateway from clients after 502s. Some autoscaling kicked in but we hit a cold-start delay for fallback runners.

jake (support): Customer impact: Support queue spiked. Notified a handful of paying tenants with high throughput — some report degraded chat responses and timeouts. No SLA breaches yet but trending.

kevin (cs): I'll start drafting a short status update for affected accounts. We need ETA for mitigation before public notice.

alex (oncall): Triage plan: 1) Reduce pressure: route traffic away from us-west1 to us-east1 (if compatible), 2) Enable model fallback to a small quantized variant for non-critical requests, 3) Restart problematic GPU nodes with kernel driver re-init and hold them out of LB, 4) Hotfix model_runner to hard-fail large allocations instead of OOMing if quick patch exists. Assign tasks: @dave do routing, @sam implement fallback and restart plan, @olivia handle node rehab, @maria monitor and collect traces.

sam (eng-runtime): Working on a graceful fallback flag. Quick config change to gateway to map requests to quant-ggml-1 when model size > threshold for busy nodes. Pushing config:```json
{
  "route_policy": "fallback_on_error",
  "fallback_model": "quant-ggml-1",
  "max_retry": 1
}
```
Applying now to canary route.

maria (sre): I've paused autoscaling thresholds temporarily to avoid spinning new pods onto affected nodes. Also added extra scraping for GPU memory and page faults.

olivia (eng-infra): Taking 3 nodes (us-west1-gpu-07..09) out of rotation. Performing driver reflash and full memtest. ETA 18m.

dave (eng-platform): Reroute started: diverting 40% of traffic to us-east1 and 20% to dedicated reserved pools; 40% remains on us-west1 until fallbacks confirmed. Observed immediate drop in 5xx from 12% -> 6% in first 2m.

jake (support): Notifying impacted tenants: "We're seeing transient 5xx affecting smaller subset; mitigation in progress; next update in 30m".

sam (eng-runtime): Canary config applied. Observed successful calls using quant-ggml-1 on canary: mean latency +20ms, success rate moved to 98% for canary traffic. Rolling to live with 25% fallback routing for non-critical endpoints.

alex (oncall): Good. Next: try to stabilize us-west nodes by restarting model_runner with limited memory cap to avoid large single-request allocations. Sam, can we add an allocation guard?

sam (eng-runtime): Quick patch added to runtime: if request allocation > 512MB chunk -> return 503 with header X-Fallback-Suggest and avoid OOM. Deploying hotpatch to canary.```
--- deployment command ---
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/model-runner-canary
```

maria (sre): Hotpatch deployed to canary. Monitoring. Node rehab still ongoing. Kernel logs show no further watchdog resets on 2/3 nodes after driver reflash.

dave (eng-platform): Also enabled short-circuit retries at gateway to do 1 retry with exponential backoff to reduce client retry storm. Config snippet:```
retry_on: gateway-5xx
max_retries: 1
backoff_ms: 200
```

kevin (cs): Sending interim note to 10 accounts flagged as high-priority. We'll include description of mitigation and expected next update in 30m.

olivia (eng-infra): Node us-west1-gpu-07 passed memtest and back in rotation (drained then rejoined). us-west1-gpu-08 showing a stale ffmpeg process locking memory; cleared and rebooting.

sam (eng-runtime): Observed one root cause thread: sudden large prompt batches (customers hitting long sequences) causing single-request allocation spikes that overflow quantized memory path and trigger fallback into dense kernel path then OOM on heavy attention matrices. We'll add per-request token limits + smarter batching.

alex (oncall): Action items: - Short term: keep fallback routing and limited retries, rehab nodes, rollback any problematic model version - Mid term: enforce per-request limits and allocation caps in runtime, add early reject for large-batch requests - Communicate: CS post, public status if impact continues >30m.

maria (sre): Current metrics (T+18m): global 5xx down to 2.1%, error tail mainly on legacy endpoints that still hit full model. We'll keep monitoring.

jake (support): Support queue trending down. No new P1s.

alex (oncall): I'll keep channel open for the next 60m. If 5xx stays <1% and nodes stable, we'll move to recovery and write post-incident notes. Great work everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident channel created: #inc-6187654321. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-runtime-oom. Incident severity set to SEV2.

sam (eng-runtime): Follow-up: I'll open a GH ticket for runtime hardening (allocation guard, per-request caps, fallback heuristics), and attach logs + core dumps.

kevin (cs): I'll coordinate customer follow-ups and summarize impact timeline for accounting.

olivia (eng-infra): Nodes 07/08/09 fully rehabbed by T+52m. No data corruption found. Scheduling deeper hardware diag in low-traffic window.

alex (oncall): Closing on-call handoff: @sam will lead postmortem, @maria to own monitoring changes, @dave to follow up on routing defaults, @olivia hardware check. Thanks all.

maria (sre): Marking channel for incident review. Please add any missing evidence links.```
